Turning to Yemen, the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warns that hostilities are forcing people to flee their homes, driving civilian casualties and putting already stretched humanitarian operations under growing pressure. At least 18,000 households, or 125,000 people, have been displaced since the start of the month. The toll on civilians is increasing. Between September 1st and today, our colleagues at the UN Human Rights Office have verified 40 civilian casualties, eight people killed and 32 others injured. Women and children account for half of those killed and more than half of those injured. We and our humanitarian partners continue to respond despite extremely difficult operating conditions. As of September 12, they have provided aid to thousands of households, but supplies are critically low and funding is falling short of needs. Humanitarian access and movement remain severely constrained due to insecurity. Humanitarian movements into and within several locations on the west coast remain suspended. while key roads are restricted or impassable.
